_notes: Ground truth established by reading the extracted PDF text (data/extracted). 'key_facts' is a list of groups; EVERY group must match (case-insensitive regex, any alternative) in the answer text. 'support' lists the paper section and PDF page range that states the facts; a cited passage must come from the same paper and overlap those pages +/-1 (table floats make section/page attribution slightly imprecise). 'forbidden' regexes mark wrong claims. 'refusal_acceptable' marks false-premise questions for which refusing is also a defensible outcome.

Q01.expected_answer: h = 8 parallel attention heads, each with dk = dv = dmodel/h = 64.

Q02.expected_answer: N = 6 identical layers; each has a multi-head self-attention sub-layer and a position-wise fully connected feed-forward sub-layer.

Q03.expected_answer: Sine and cosine functions of different frequencies; chosen because the authors hypothesized it would let the model easily learn to attend by relative positions (and may extrapolate to longer sequences). Learned embeddings gave nearly identical results.

Q04.expected_answer: Adam optimizer (beta1 = 0.9, beta2 = 0.98, epsilon = 1e-9) with warmup_steps = 4000.

Q05.expected_answer: One machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs; base models 100,000 steps (~12 hours); big models 300,000 steps (3.5 days).

Q06.expected_answer: 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German; 41.0 BLEU on English-to-French (the abstract says 41.8, the Results section 41.0 - the paper is internally inconsistent, either is accepted).

Q07.expected_answer: Extend the Transformer to other input/output modalities (images, audio, video), investigate local restricted attention for large inputs/outputs, and make generation less sequential.

Q08.expected_answer: A 4-layer Transformer (dmodel = 1024) trained on the WSJ portion of the Penn Treebank (~40K sentences), plus a semi-supervised setting with ~17M sentences.

Q09.expected_answer: A theoretical latency of 160 ms and 200 ms in practice.

Q10.expected_answer: Moshi predicts time-aligned text tokens of its own speech as a prefix to the audio (semantic) tokens, which improves the linguistic quality of generated speech while staying compatible with streaming.

Q11.expected_answer: 12.5 Hz frame rate, 1.1 kbps, Q = 8 quantizers (codebook size 2048).

Q12.expected_answer: Helium is a 7B-parameter text LLM pretrained on 2.1T tokens of public English data.

Q13.expected_answer: The Depth Transformer has 6 layers, dimension 1024 and 16 attention heads. (The Transformer paper's 8 heads is a different model.)

Q15.expected_answer: Instead of a single 8-level RVQ, semantic information is distilled into a plain VQ and an RVQ with 7 levels runs in parallel, their outputs summed. It avoids forcing the first RVQ level to trade audio quality for phonetic discriminability.

Q16.expected_answer: Encoder network(s), a main network, and decoder network(s).

Q17.expected_answer: It guides the model toward a target compression ratio and prevents trivial solutions (keeping everything or compressing too much); N controls the target compression ratio.

Q18.expected_answer: It computes cosine similarity between adjacent encoder outputs (via query/key projections); low similarity means a semantic shift and gives a high boundary probability.

Q19.expected_answer: The current implementation may be up to about 2x slower than an isotropic model during training (and memory use is dynamic).

Q20.expected_answer: A 100B-token subset of FineWeb-Edu; tokenizer-free models process 8192 byte sequences.

Q21.expected_answer: A one-stage byte-level H-Net outperforms a strong BPE Transformer (compute- and data-matched); a multi-stage H-Net matches the token-based Transformer of twice its size.

Q22.expected_answer: The Transformer paper encodes text with byte-pair encoding (shared ~37000-token vocabulary) - a fixed tokenizer; H-Net removes tokenization and models raw bytes end to end with learned dynamic chunking.

Q23.expected_answer: Mimi operates at 12.5 Hz; H-Net's dynamic chunking learns content- and context-dependent boundaries (via cosine similarity between adjacent vectors).

Q24.expected_answer: Transformer: 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs. H-Net: a 100B-token subset of FineWeb-Edu.

Q25.refusal_criteria: Must refuse. The only Nvidia mention is 'NVIDIA P100 GPUs' in the Transformer paper (5.2, p.7): lexically relevant, but it is hardware, not revenue. Any numeric revenue answer is wrong.

Q26.refusal_criteria: Must refuse. BLEU and WMT 2014 appear only in the Transformer paper; attributing them to Moshi is wrong.

Q27.expected_answer: The premise is false: the authors did not attempt a 3-stage H-Net (they tried 0, 1 and 2 stages).

Q28.expected_answer: The premise is false: the Transformer dispenses with recurrence and convolutions entirely and relies solely on attention.

Q29.expected_answer: None - the H-Net paper never mentions Inner Monologue; the premise is unsupported.
Q29.refusal_criteria: Must refuse (or at minimum not describe any such mechanism). Inner Monologue appears only in the Moshi paper.

Q30.expected_answer: None - general knowledge, not in the library.
Q30.refusal_criteria: Must refuse. 'France' and 'Paris' appear in a Moshi appendix example conversation (about d'Artagnan, p.63), but that text does not state that Paris is the capital. Answering 'Paris' uses outside knowledge.

Q31.refusal_criteria: Must refuse. GPT-4 appears only as a baseline name in Moshi's toxicity table (6.1, p.36).
